definition: Muscarine is a cholinergic agonist that, in this study, was used to partly mimic an aroused-like brain state in rat medial prefrontal cortex tissue. It triggered prolonged depolarising plateau potentials and spiking in layer 2/3 pyramidal cells, indicating a role in modulating cortical activity linked to consciousness and working memory research.

reasons: The definition adds an unsupported inference that muscarine has a role in modulating cortical activity linked to consciousness and working memory research; the packet only says muscarine was bath-applied to partly mimic an “aroused-like” state and that layer 2/3 pyramidal cells are important in theories of those functions.
The phrasing shifts from the packet’s specific in vitro slice preparation to a broader claim about a brain state and cortical activity that is not directly supported.

The definition’s concluding claim that the results “indicat[e] a role in modulating cortical activity linked to consciousness and working memory research” goes beyond what the packet explicitly supports. The packet states that the authors used muscarine to partly mimic an “aroused-like” state and that L2/3 pyramidal cells are important for access consciousness and working memory according to leading theories, but it does not explicitly conclude that muscarine itself “indicates” that role.
